Halifax's traffic problem is growing alongside South Dartmouth's neighbourhoods

2026-09-26 The Canadian Press (via Narcity) TomTom Traffic Index, Halifax, traffic congestion, Canada, Dartmouth, transit, GIS, open data, urban planning, commute
Read the source article

Quick summary

Halifax ranked third worst in Canada for traffic congestion in 2025 according to the TomTom Traffic Index, with drivers losing 111 hours to rush hour — more than Toronto commuters — as fast-tracked housing development in South Dartmouth outpaces transportation infrastructure.

Key takeaways

  • Halifax city centre ranked third worst in Canada for traffic congestion in 2025 per the TomTom Traffic Index, behind Vancouver and Toronto
  • Drivers in Halifax Regional Municipality lost 111 hours to rush hour, more than Toronto's 100 hours despite Toronto being 14× larger
  • Average daily traffic on Pleasant Street climbed 8% between December 2021 and May 2025 (10,987 to 11,828 vehicles/day)
  • Traffic counts on Mount Hope Avenue rose nearly 5% in one year (15,392 to 16,139 vehicles/day)
  • Nearly 1,800 residential units approved through Special Planning Areas (SPA) in Mount Hope Village and Opal Ridge
  • 518 collisions on Pleasant Street between 2018 and 2026 resulted in three fatalities, per HRM open data portal
  • Route 5 transit passenger overload incidents tripled from 17 in 2022 to 57 in 2024
  • HRM proposed a $70-million Halifax Transit Core Service Plan changing 37% of bus routes
